projectName: Suite Identity: Tailnet Sign-In and Passkey Step-Up
description: Replace per-app passphrases, PINs, and name pickers with one household identity. The tailnet login (asserted by Tailscale Serve) identifies the member on every request with zero interaction. Home Base keeps the household directory and runs a suite passkey service that sensitive apps use for step-up checks. Sensitive apps and Home Base admin each get their own hostname so a compromised sibling app cannot drive them from the browser. Every app keeps its existing local auth as the standalone fallback.

timing.plannedEarliestExecution: After the Feature-4 Serve publishing lane is stable on production hosts
timing.gatingCondition: Spikes 1 and 2 passed on a test VM on 2026-10-23; spikes 3 and 3b on 2026-10-25/26 (evidence.spike3, evidence.spike3b) on Tailscale 1.102.4. SID-001 may start. Each production host must run Tailscale ≥ 1.102.4, have its Serve topology confirmed read-only, and have its tailnet policy and existing service-host approvals reviewed (runbook section 2) before SID-001 executes there. The browser-isolation rules added after spike 3 (D20, D21, D22) are tested in SID-003/SID-005 and the SID-008 rehearsal

principles: The tailnet login is the person, but only for logins the administrator has admitted to the directory. Tagged devices, unknown logins, and externally shared users get no identity
Members who never had a password get no new friction; apps that had passphrases trade them for nothing (tailnet-only) or a passkey tap (sensitive apps)
Identity headers are trusted only when the only possible path to the app is Tailscale Serve → a root-only nginx socket for that hostname → the app's own socket
The tailnet identity is ambient, like a cookie: every mutating request needs an exact Origin match and a JSON content type, and authorization runs before any mutation or step-up prompt
One hostname per trust boundary: low-friction apps share the suite hostname; each sensitive app and Home Base admin gets its own
Passkey checks never request the PRF extension; they prove presence only, so synced passkeys from third-party providers work on iOS
Classify credentials from what the authenticator proves: only a credential with verified attestation from a pinned hardware vendor root counts as a hardware key
The administrator is a Home Base designation, not an app role; apps keep parent/kid
Every app can still run standalone with its existing local auth
No acting as another member; no shared-device mode
Prefer the simplest storage: directory in Home Base state, a snapshot file Home Base owns and apps can only read (integrity from file ownership, not signatures)

decisions.D1: Tailnet identity is the suite identity, keyed on the tailnet's stable user ID. nginx resolves it on every request with auth_request to a Home Base identity endpoint (whois on Serve's client IP) and passes it as X-Sovereign-User-Id; the whois login must equal Tailscale-User-Login. If the lookup fails or disagrees, the request carries no identity (fail closed). The login string is display only
decisions.D2: No shared devices; tagged devices get no identity. Hosts that serve the suite must be tagged; the planner refuses tailnet mode on a user-owned node, where local processes would arrive as the node's owner
decisions.D3: No impersonation; a parent who needs a kid's view uses the kid's device
decisions.D4: Passkey checks only in sensitive apps (finance, estate documents, trading, Bitcoin accounting); previously passwordless apps get no new friction
decisions.D5: Multi-host federation deferred; each host is its own household instance keyed on tailnet identities
decisions.D7: Kid views in sensitive apps stay at tailnet level where the app already scopes kid data server-side
decisions.D8: Home Base admin requires a passkey: 8h session plus an every-time attested hardware key for privileged plans and administrator actions; the admin passphrase is used only in the setup and recovery states (D16)
decisions.D9: Operator apps (trading, Bitcoin accounting) use a 24h passkey session window
decisions.D10: 'administrator' is a Home Base-only flag, separate from parent; only an administrator can grant it; never synced between hosts
decisions.D11: Multiple credentials per member (synced passkeys and hardware keys side by side); the administrator must hold ≥2 credentials including ≥1 attested hardware key, and Home Base refuses (transactionally) to remove the last one
decisions.D12: One assurance policy matrix (assurancePolicy below) defines every protected action's level and credential kind; apps and Home Base enforce it through the shared library, not ad hoc
decisions.D13: The shared library and passkey code live in a new public repo, sovereignAuth, Node package at the root. Apps take it as a git dependency pinned to a commit (package-lock.json). A Python package under python/ is added when the first Python app migrates (wave 3), and must pass the same conformance vectors. Hosts need no GitHub credentials
decisions.D14: Separate hostnames via Tailscale Services, qualified by household instance: svc:<instance>-home (low-friction apps), svc:<instance>-homebase (admin), svc:<instance>-<app> per sensitive app. Each service has exactly one approved host, and that is a tailnet-policy boundary (spike 3b): any approved second host becomes a standby, receives a valid certificate for the service hostname, and takes all traffic and members' identity headers when the first host stops serving. So: (1) each serving host gets its own tag (tag:<instance>-host), owned only by the administrator, held by no other device; (2) every approver rule that can match a service resolves only to that tag, or the service is approved by hand; (3) tightening approvers does not revoke approvals that already exist, so the service's approved hosts are reviewed and stale ones removed after every policy change; (4) Tailnet Lock is recommended, because it keeps a stolen or leaked tagged auth key from adding a host without a trusted signature. Home Base verifies this as described in D23; its publish guard is a second check, not the boundary, because a hostile host can run the Tailscale CLI directly. Each service targets its own root-only nginx socket and serves only its own allowlisted mounts
decisions.D15: Credential kinds: synced, device-bound, hardware. 'hardware' requires attestation verified against pinned vendor root certificates shipped in sovereignAuth; flags alone never make a credential hardware
decisions.D16: Bootstrap states: setup → active → recovery (SID-004). Recovery is the only exception to the credential rules: the recorded administrator (same stable user ID) plus the passphrase may enroll replacement administrator credentials without an existing hardware check. Recovery ends when the administrator again meets D11 and completes a fresh hardware ceremony
decisions.D17: The RP ID is the tailnet domain, fixed when the first credential is enrolled. Because every hostname in the tailnet could otherwise start a ceremony for that RP ID, ceremonies run only on the Home Base hostname and sensitive-app hostnames, never on svc:<instance>-home. Each challenge is stored with its origin (the hostname that issued it), member, purpose (step-up, enroll, revoke, or an action), audience, and action context; finish verifies against that stored record, once, and refuses any mismatch. clientDataJSON must have crossOrigin false and no topOrigin. A ceremony's cookie or token is valid only on its own hostname. The RP ID is not configurable per host. The only change is a tailnet rename, which rebinds it, orphans every credential, bumps the global epoch, and enters recovery (runbook section 7)
decisions.D18: Snapshot trust comes from file ownership: Home Base writes it into a directory it owns that apps can read but not write. Apps open it by descriptor (no symlinks) and refuse it unless the file and directory are owned by the Home Base user and writable by no one else. It is rewritten on every change and every 30 s; apps re-check at most every 5 s and refuse it when older than 120 s
decisions.D19: Token redemption goes over a per-app Home Base socket, /run/sovereign-identity/<app>.sock (owner Home Base user, group the app's user, 0660), so the socket path authenticates the calling app. Redemption fails closed on timeout or Home Base restart
decisions.D20: All service hostnames in one tailnet are a single browser site: ts.net is a public suffix, so <service>.<tailnet>.ts.net names are same-site to each other (spike 3: Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site; a Domain=<tailnet>.ts.net cookie set on one hostname is sent to the others, even with SameSite=Strict). SameSite gives no isolation between them. Isolation therefore rests on: exact-Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin checks on mutations; __Host- prefixed cookies (which a sibling cannot set) bound to their hostname; side-effect-free GET/HEAD, including pages that must not mutate on load from URL parameters; on sensitive and Home Base hostnames, refusing every request except same-origin ones and top-level document navigations (GET, Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate, Sec-Fetch-Dest: document), and refusing requests with missing or malformed Sec-Fetch-Site (supported clients: iOS/iPadOS and macOS Safari 16.4+, which covers the iOS web wrapper; Chrome and Edge 80+; Firefox 90+; older clients are refused on those hostnames; health checks use the app socket, not nginx); and Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none' on every response from those hostnames, including /_sovereign/auth/
decisions.D21: Credential management lives on the Home Base hostname only: enrolling, labeling, and revoking credentials, and redeeming enrollment grants, for every member, not just the administrator. Members with sensitive apps get tcp:443 to svc:<instance>-homebase for this; Home Base admin routes there still require the administrator. Sensitive-app hostnames run only step-up ceremonies for their own app. /_sovereign/auth/ is not mounted on svc:<instance>-home at all, so low-friction apps get no ceremonies and no assurance cookies
decisions.D22: OAuth and other external callbacks follow one contract, and it is the only exception to D20's rule that pages never act on load from URL parameters: the callback GET renders a landing page that changes nothing and needs no cookie; the page then sends only the code and state, once, in a same-origin JSON POST to that app's completion route, which passes the mutation guard. The completion route refuses unless the state is single-use, unexpired (≤10 minutes), and bound to the initiating member, hostname, and a __Host- correlation cookie (SameSite=Strict; withheld on the cross-site redirect, sent on the same-origin POST); PKCE wherever the provider supports it. No other route may act on URL parameters at load. An app that cannot follow this contract stays entirely in local mode; there is no per-route mixed mode
decisions.D23: Service-host verification. The local host cannot see standby hosts or the tailnet policy (spike 3b: an approved standby showed no routes until failover), and a correct policy does not prove there is no stale approval (spike 3b: the old approval survived the policy change). So the deciding evidence is the service's host inventory, not the policy. Automatic: with a Tailscale API credential limited to reading services and devices (the listServiceHosts endpoint documents the services and devices:core scopes; SID-001 confirms the read-only variants suffice, and if they do not, the household uses the confirmation branch rather than a broader credential), the planner lists each service's hosts at publish time and daily and passes only if exactly one host is approved (approved:auto or approved:manual) and its stable device ID is this device's; any other approved host, an inventory that is missing, partial, or unparseable, or an API error makes the service unverified. The policy and tag checks (this device alone holds the host tag, its owners are the administrator only, every approver rule that can match the service resolves only to that tag, including rules matching service tags) still run, and their failure is reported as a warning to fix before the next approval goes wrong. Confirmation (no credential, or read-only scopes insufficient): the administrator confirms, from the console's Services page, that each service lists exactly one approved host, names it, and has removed every other host's approval; Home Base shows the service as 'confirmed by administrator', never 'verified'. The confirmation needs an every-time hardware key once Home Base is active, and is repeated on every publish and every 30 days. Bootstrap: in the setup state (D16), before any hardware key exists, the administrator may publish svc:<instance>-homebase alone with a passphrase-session confirmation so the enrollment surface exists; no app may enter tailnet mode and no other service may be published until Home Base is active and the hardware-key confirmation (or automatic verification) has passed for svc:<instance>-homebase again. Unverified or unconfirmed services refuse tailnet-mode changes (fail closed); running services keep their last state with a warning. Confirmed 2026-10-27: a trust credential with services:read, devices:core:read and policy_file:read reads listServiceHosts, getService, the device list and the policy, and a write attempt with it is refused (403), so automatic verification needs no write scope. Publishing is gated on "no other host is approved" (this host appears in the inventory only after it advertises); tailnet mode is gated on "verified". Before the household directory exists (lifecycle 'none', before SID-004) no app can trust identity and no hardware key exists, so services may be published under the publish gate and nothing may enter tailnet mode; the setup-state bootstrap rule applies from SID-004 on

levels.tailnet: An admitted member's identity headers on the request; no cookie needed
levels.session: An assurance cookie for this hostname within the app's window, with the member's current epoch and the household's current global epoch
levels.recent: An assurance cookie whose auth_time is ≤5 minutes old
levels.every-time: A single-use action token from a fresh ceremony, bound to this exact request

matrix.action: Use a low-friction app (dinner, fasting, help desk, calendar)
Link external accounts, export data, change a member's parent/kid role
A member adds or removes their own credential (Home Base hostname only, D21)
matrix.kind: any (or an enrollment grant for a member with no credentials)

matrix.action: Administrator adds or removes an administrator credential
Privileged Home Base plans (install, repair, adopt, update, uninstall, restore), config changes, publishing changes, rotating secrets

evidence.spike1: Serve adds Tailscale-User-Login/Name and replaces client-forged copies; correct identity from macOS, iOS web wrapper, and a kid's Windows PC; tagged host gets no identity headers. nginx on a 0700 root unix socket refuses non-root local users. Found: nginx on 0.0.0.0 blocks Serve's tailnet :443 bind; apps bind 0.0.0.0 despite catalog upstreamBind; forged X-Sovereign-* passes unless nginx overwrites it; absolute redirects leak http://localhost behind the socket
evidence.spike2: Passkey enroll/step-up with 1Password (desktop and iPhone), Apple Passwords, and a USB-C YubiKey; tailnet-level RP ID accepted by Chrome and Safari; signed assurance cookie rejected on identity mismatch or tamper; single-use action tokens reject reuse, wrong action, wrong kind, wrong member, and expiry (in-memory, single process only); a non-administrator member enrolled a synced passkey, passed session and recent checks, and was refused the administrator action with 403 before any prompt. Limits: hardware classification came from flags (not proof; see D15); parent/kid roles not exercised; one origin only. Found: apps on loopback TCP can be reached directly with forged headers; all apps share one service user
evidence.spike3: Test VM, Tailscale 1.102.4, 2026-10-25, host tagged, two instance-qualified test services. Passed: Serve identity headers and unix-socket targets work on Tailscale Services; each service reaches only its own nginx socket and allowlisted mounts (others 404; a hostname sent to the other service's address gets 421); Serve overwrites client-sent X-Forwarded-For (single and multiple values) and X-Forwarded-Host; the nginx auth_request whois lookup returns the stable user ID and ignores forged X-Sovereign-*, Tailscale-User-*, X-Forwarded-* headers; stopping the identity endpoint fails requests closed; a non-root local user cannot connect to the nginx sockets. On the user-owned node, any local process (even nobody) reached the host's own Serve URL as the owner (confirms D2; a self-IP guard in the identity endpoint refused it); once tagged, local requests carry no login. A user-owned node is refused as a service host ("service hosts must be tagged nodes"). A YubiKey packed attestation verified against the pinned Yubico U2F root and was rejected with a wrong root; with no roots loaded the library skips chain checks (why SID-005 refuses that); a software authenticator's direct attestation was rejected under pinned roots and its none-attestation credential classified device-bound, where the spike-2 flag rule would have said hardware. Cross-hostname from the home service to a sensitive one: credentialed reads were unreadable by the page (CORS), a JSON POST stopped at the preflight, and a form POST reached the app with the member's identity, the sibling's Origin, and Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site. The test app had no guards, so this shows what arrives, not that it is refused; server-side refusal (D20) is tested in SID-003 and SID-008. Found: hostnames are same-site (D20) and cookie tossing works; each new service hostname takes 35–40 s on first request while its certificate is issued; a service host cannot resolve its own service names through tailnet DNS. Not tested: a second tagged host trying to take over a service (spike 3b). The spike's own policy auto-approved services for a tag, which any second host with that tag would also satisfy (why D14 now requires per-host tags)
evidence.spike3b: Test VM, 2026-10-26, Tailnet Lock enabled. A second node joined with a tagged, pre-approved auth key and was locked out until a trusted key signed it. Once signed and sharing the first host's tag, which the policy used as a service approver, its advertisement of the service was auto-approved: it became a standby with no visible routes, obtained a valid certificate for the service hostname, and answered every request once the first host drained. After the approvers were changed to a tag only the first host holds, the second node's existing approval remained and it still took over on drain; the first host lost its approvals until it received the new tag. After the second node withdrew and advertised again, it was not approved, and with the first host drained the service stopped answering instead of failing over. Conclusions are in D14 and D23

evidence.sid001Rehearsal: Test VM, Tailscale 1.102.4, 2026-10-27, instance "rehearsal", per-host tag with per-service autoApprovers, read-only trust credential. Through the real executor: cutover (socket gateway, tmpfiles, identity socket dir, app snippets migrated to <service>--<app>.conf), publish of homebase, home and source (each verified via listServiceHosts once approved; certificate warm-up 34-36 s each), rollback (TCP gateway, snippets re-rendered for TCP, Serve restored to the pre-cutover snapshot, node entries kept), and a second cutover. From a member device: each mount only on its own hostname (404 elsewhere), a hostname sent to another service's address gets 421 both ways, relative mount redirects, frame-ancestors on every Home Base and sensitive response including 404s, forged X-Sovereign-*/Tailscale-User-*/X-Forwarded-* headers never reach the app, Home Base stopped = 500. On the host: no TCP listener, nobody cannot reach the nginx or identity sockets, a local process requesting its own public URL gets no identity. The identity resolver on real data returned the member's stable user ID (equal to whois UserProfile.ID) only for a matching login, never for the host's own IPv4/IPv6, a tagged peer, a mismatched login, or without a directory. Found and fixed: app snippets must follow the host's ingress mode (otherwise installs on pre-cutover hosts write an include that does not exist); /run/homebase belongs to the executor and must stay root-owned (the identity socket moved to /run/homebase-identity); the executor protocol's outer field list and execute.js's bootstrap-only layout exemption refused the new host actions; the live API answers {} for a service without hosts and names host IDs nodeId; `tailscale serve set-raw` with get-config output wipes node-level Serve entries (set-config --all does not). Not yet rehearsed: a second tagged host (spike 3b procedure), the admin UI path, an interrupted cutover (SID-008)

userStories.title: Identity-safe ingress: per-service Serve → root-only nginx sockets
acceptanceCriteria: Both deployment paths change together: the publish planner and the root executor (executor/handlers.js nginx rendering) emit the same layout; a later install, repair, or update never reintroduces a TCP listener

Each published service (svc:<instance>-home, svc:<instance>-homebase, one svc:<instance>-<app> per sensitive app) targets its own socket /run/sovereign-serve/<service>.sock; the directory is created at boot by tmpfiles.d, 0700 root:root

The publisher checks endpoint conflicts per service (tcp:443 on a different service is not a conflict), verifies each service is advertised and approved for this host only, and refuses to publish a service another host already serves. The planner refuses tailnet mode for a service until D23 verification passes (API) or the administrator has confirmed it (no API), and fails closed when the configured API cannot be evaluated

Each server block includes only its own service's mounts (sovereign-home.d/<service>/); /_sovereign/auth/ is added on the Home Base and sensitive-app blocks only, never on svc:<instance>-home (D21); admin routes exist only on the homebase service; a request whose X-Forwarded-Host doesn't match the block's hostname gets 421
Each nginx server block listens only on its socket (no TCP 80/443 for the suite), sets absolute_redirect off, and gives every mount an explicit 'location = /mount { return 301 /mount/; }'

A shared identity snippet is included inside every proxy location (nginx drops inherited proxy_set_header once a location sets its own). It runs auth_request to the Home Base identity endpoint (D1) and sets X-Sovereign-User-Id, X-Sovereign-Login, and X-Sovereign-Name from its answer and Serve's Tailscale-User-* headers, always overwriting client copies (absent ⇒ omitted); Host comes from X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto from Serve

Apps and Home Base read identity only from X-Sovereign-*; a forged X-Sovereign-* or Tailscale-User-* header is replaced or dropped on every location, including sidecar routes (e.g. the bug tracker's MCP location)
Planner refuses tailnet identity for an app whose upstream is still TCP, and on a user-owned (untagged) serving node; it says why

Feature-4 verification replaces the 'nginx listener on tcp:443' check with 'nginx sockets present, root-only, and each service targets its own'; readiness checks in src/operations/policy.js no longer assume ports

Rollback is dependency-ordered: the planner refuses to restore any TCP ingress while any app is in tailnet mode; the rollback plan first returns every app to local mode, then restores the saved Serve and nginx config

Publishing a service waits until its certificate is issued (first request takes 35–40 s) and verifies the hostname answers before any app on it switches to tailnet mode; the check runs on the serving host with explicit service-IP resolution, because a service host cannot resolve its own service names
The identity endpoint refuses lookups for the host's own tailnet addresses, IPv4 and IPv6, as a backstop to D2
Sensitive and Home Base blocks send Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none' on every response, including /_sovereign/auth/ (D20)
userStories.testStrategy: Planner, publisher, and executor rendering tests (snippet in every location, per-service allowlists, per-service conflict detection); VM rehearsal of the spike-1 and spike-3 checks per hostname: every mount requested on every other hostname is refused; forged and missing headers on every route; forged X-Forwarded-For; local bypass refused; local process against the public URL; tagged host no identity; redirects stay on the hostname; D23 evaluator tests against recorded API responses: a second approved host (auto or manual), a not-approved second host (passes), this device missing from the inventory, a partial or unparseable inventory, an API error, and a 403 from read-only scopes are all handled as specified; policy warnings for a shared approver tag, a second device holding the host tag, a non-administrator tag owner, and an extra matching approver rule; on the VM with a real read-only credential, confirm which scopes listServiceHosts needs; the bootstrap path publishes only svc:<instance>-homebase in setup and refuses every other publish and tailnet-mode change until active
implementationNotes: Host paths use the bare service key (/run/sovereign-serve/<key>.sock, sovereign-home.d/<key>--<app>.conf) so they never depend on the instance; service names and hostnames carry it

The executor records the cutover in /var/lib/homebase-executor/ingress.json (root, 0600); every later gateway or app-snippet write follows that mode, and it never writes a TCP gateway over a socket one
App snippets are rendered for the host's ingress mode: TCP-gateway hosts keep the pre-SID-001 headers; cutover and rollback re-render every installed app's snippet

The identity socket lives in /run/homebase-identity (0750 homebase:www-data, created by the cutover's tmpfiles entry); Home Base starts listening when the directory appears. /run/homebase is the executor's and stays root-owned
Serve is changed only with `tailscale serve set-config --all`; the pre-cutover services are snapshotted on first change and restored by rollback

After cutover, Open links and each app's URL env values (including OAuth redirects and local font URLs) use the app's service hostname; an app update after cutover refreshes them, and OAuth providers need the new callback URLs
Every server block serves /_sovereign/fonts/ from the shared assets, replacing the legacy operator snippet
Rollback is refused by Home Base while any installation is in tailnet mode, and by the executor while any app's own .env has SOVEREIGN_IDENTITY_MODE=tailnet

userStories.title: App listen contract and per-app ownership
acceptanceCriteria: Catalog gains a listen contract (runtime.listen = unix) and renders SOVEREIGN_LISTEN=unix:/run/sovereign-apps/<id>/app.sock; apps not yet supporting it render HOST=127.0.0.1 and stay in local mode
Socket directory /run/sovereign-apps/<id>: owner = the app's service user, group = nginx's group, mode 2750; socket 0660; recreated on restart. App service users are never members of nginx's group

Sensitive apps run as their own service user, and the whole ownership graph moves with them: checkout and its parent path (root-owned 0755 parents), code, .env, storage, backups, dependency installs and caches, timers and workers. The shared service user cannot write, replace, or read any of them
The executor installs dependencies and runs migrations as the app's own user, writes .env as root with the app's user as owner (0600), and stores that app's backups 0700 under its user

nginx upstreams keep each app's URI behavior: mount-preserving apps (trading, Bitcoin accounting) use 'proxy_pass http://unix:<sock>;' (no URI), prefix-stripping apps use 'proxy_pass http://unix:<sock>:/;'
Health checks and post-install verification work over the socket
userStories.testStrategy: Install-planner and executor tests for env/unit/nginx/ownership rendering; VM checks: the shared service user is refused by a sensitive app's socket and cannot read or write its checkout, .env, or backups; nested APIs, redirects, static assets, and OAuth callbacks work under the D22 contract (read-only landing, same-origin JSON POST, single-use state bound to member and hostname) for one mount-preserving and one prefix-stripping app
implementationNotes: Sensitive apps (network.dedicatedHostname) run as sovereign-<service key>, home /var/lib/sovereign-home/<app id>/home; the checkout's owner decides who an app runs as, so installs from before SID-002 keep sovereign until the one-time move-user action (safety backup, stop, two-pass root hand-over through no-follow descriptors with the checkout last, .env and units rewritten, start). The move is one way
apps/ and backups/ are root-owned 0755; each own-user app's checkout, storage, home and backup directory is 0700 and its .env 0600. identity.ensure-user refuses a user in nginx's group

runtime.listen = unix renders SOVEREIGN_LISTEN; every other app gets HOST=127.0.0.1, and the other mode's key is removed on every render. A tmpfiles entry keeps /run/sovereign-apps/<id> at 2750 <user>:www-data across reboots. Sidecars stay on loopback TCP

Home Base can't reach a socket, so readiness waits and the health monitor (including the onboarding payload) use the executor's app-probe request; app-identity reports who an app runs as for the Runs as card
Ingress verification adds apps-loopback-only: any catalog app or sidecar port bound beyond loopback fails it

App support: familyPulse #8 and homeSource #45 (lib/listen.js, prefix-stripping), helm #67 and bitcoinAccounting #6 (listen.py, mount-preserving; the launcher loads .env before choosing where to listen). Seven Node apps were fixed to honour HOST instead of binding every interface

Rehearsed on the test VM 2026-10-28: Home Source moved in place, then switched TCP to socket; Pulse, Helm and Bitcoin Accounting installed fresh. The shared user, Home Base and other apps' users were refused at each socket; on the moved app the shared user was also denied its code, .env, data and backups; update, backup and restart worked after the move; pages, redirects, assets, nested APIs and OAuth callback routes worked from a member device for both URI styles. The D22 callback contract itself is app behavior, checked when each app enters tailnet mode

Code review (PR #16) took eight external rounds, all on the root hand-over: directories are locked root 0700 before they are read; hardlinks owned by others are left alone; a root marker makes an interrupted move resumable and blocks other plans; copies are staged per tree; mounts are refused by mount table and mount ID; restore re-applies the listen mode. Accepted limitation: a root process mounting inside a tree mid-move

Production rollout 2026-10-28 on both hosts, behind the old TCP gateway (no cutover). Fixed from it: probe fallback to the port until the app is updated, marker-aware lock drift, wire-once page actions (PR #17); a move keeps the existing database password, and takes a legacy shared-user data parent back for root (PR #18)

Open: Helm on DATABASE_URL instead of HELM_DATABASE_URL; a policy warning for a service no grant reaches; a bare / redirect on sensitive hostnames; sidecars on sockets; a private mount namespace for the hand-over; the health message for an app on its port but not yet updated still says 'socket'

userStories.title: sovereignAuth core library and wire contract
acceptanceCriteria: The sovereignAuth repo exists (public, Node package at the root, tagged releases) and is installed as a commit-pinned git dependency; a Home Base install on the VM succeeds without GitHub credentials
Defines and documents the wire contract: X-Sovereign-* headers, snapshot format, assurance cookie, action token, step-up 401 body

Snapshot reader (D18): opens by descriptor without following symlinks; refuses a snapshot that is missing, not owned by the Home Base user, writable by anyone else, older than 120 s, or of a lower generation than the last one seen; re-checks at most every 5 s

Request guard: the member comes from X-Sovereign-User-Id looked up in the snapshot (never from the login alone), and the snapshot's login for that ID must match X-Sovereign-Login; unknown, disabled, or tagged ⇒ no member; app modes are 'local' or 'tailnet' only, anything else fails closed; tailnet mode refuses to start unless listening on its socket

Mutation guard (default on for every non-GET/HEAD): Origin must equal this hostname's origin (same-site is not enough, D20), content type must be application/json, Sec-Fetch-Site must be same-origin when present. GET and HEAD handlers must have no side effects (a sibling hostname's GET reaches the app with the member's identity); exports and other actions are POST

Resource isolation (on by default for sensitive apps and Home Base admin, D20): allow a request only if Sec-Fetch-Site is same-origin, or it is a top-level document navigation (GET, Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate, Sec-Fetch-Dest: document); refuse missing or malformed Sec-Fetch-Site. Pages reached by navigation never mutate on load from URL parameters

OAuth callback helper (D22): the landing route needs no cookie and changes nothing; the completion route accepts one same-origin JSON POST of code and state, refusing a missing, replayed, expired (>10 min), or mismatched state (member, hostname, or correlation cookie); PKCE when the provider supports it. It is the only helper allowed to act on URL parameters at load

requireAssurance(policyKey, {target}) reads the level and kind from the assurance policy matrix and returns step_up_required before the handler runs. Only the __Host-sv_assurance cookie is read (any other name, including a same-named cookie without the prefix, is ignored); it must match aud (this hostname), the member's epoch, and the global epoch. Every-time actions redeem the token over the app's own redemption socket (D19), passing the action and the target the app resolved before the 401, and Home Base rechecks the member's current authorization

Conformance vectors (valid, expired, wrong aud, stale epoch, replayed, wrong digest, unprefixed or tossed cookie, same-site Origin, missing or malformed Sec-Fetch-Site, framed or sibling-initiated subresource request, permitted top-level navigation) ship with the repo for any later language port
The WebAuthn helpers extracted from the estate-documents app live here (D11)
userStories.testStrategy: Library unit tests driven by the conformance vectors; mutation-guard tests for cross-site form posts (text/plain), wrong Origin, and missing Origin; browser tests from a sibling hostname, checked on the server: fetch, image, script, and iframe requests refused, a framed page blocked by frame-ancestors, a Domain cookie planted with the assurance cookie's unprefixed name ignored, a top-level navigation allowed and changing nothing; the iOS web wrapper sends Sec-Fetch-* and passes; OAuth: replayed state, state from another member or hostname, missing correlation cookie, a sibling-hostname POST to the completion route, and a completion attempt from any page other than the landing page are refused; the real iOS web wrapper passes initial navigation, subresource, mutation, and callback flows before cutover
implementationNotes: Scope (2026-10-28): the library alone has no member to resolve until SID-004 builds the directory, so SID-003 also wires Home Base to it behind a flag, enough to prove it on the test VM. Real issuance (directory, cookies, step-up, redemption server) stays in SID-004/005

API: framework-agnostic core functions over {method, url, headers} that return a decision, with thin adapters for Node's http (Home Base) and Express (the Node apps). CommonJS, Node >= 22, no build step and no install scripts (hosts run npm ci --ignore-scripts)

Tokens: Ed25519 (per the tech stack), a fixed format 'v1.<base64url payload>.<base64url signature>' with a key ID, no algorithm field (no JWT, no algorithm negotiation). Verification keys come from the snapshot
Conformance vectors are language-neutral JSON under vectors/, so the Python port (D13, wave 3) runs the same files

Home Base wiring, behind HOME_BASE_REQUEST_GUARDS=off|report|enforce (default off): sovereignAuth as a commit-pinned git dependency; the mutation guard and resource isolation on Home Base's own routes (report logs what enforce would refuse); a preview snapshot written from a static members file standing in for the directory, replaced by SID-004; and a read-only who-am-I route showing what the request guard resolved

Proven on the test VM: Home Base installs the dependency without GitHub credentials; from a sibling service hostname, fetch, image, script, iframe and form posts to Home Base admin are refused while a top-level navigation is allowed; a member device resolves to its member end to end (Serve, nginx identity, snapshot); an app's user can read the snapshot, and the reader refuses it made writable, symlinked, re-owned or stale; the iOS wrapper sends Sec-Fetch-* and passes

Library only until SID-004/005: assurance cookie and action-token verification, the redemption client (tested against a fake Home Base socket), the OAuth callback helper, and the WebAuthn helpers. The extraction from Home Source takes storage as a parameter, fixes bugBase #147 (trust the authenticator's flags, not the chosen method) and keeps PRF; Home Source adopts it in SID-005/007

userStories.title: Household directory, bootstrap, and recovery
acceptanceCriteria: Directory records per member: suite_member_id, display name, tailnet stable user ID (required; from the per-request identity lookup, D1), current login, role parent|kid, administrator flag, status, credential epoch, per-app access (default all; operator apps default administrator-only). Logins and user IDs are unique
A request whose login matches a member but whose stable user ID does not is treated as unknown; administrator rights never follow a login string to a new account

Bootstrap state machine: 'setup' (no administrator credentials) → 'active' (≥2 administrator credentials including ≥1 attested hardware key) → 'recovery' (entered only by the passphrase while active, or by the root CLI)

In 'setup', the passphrase plus the founder's tailnet identity records that identity as the first administrator and allows only enrolling administrator credentials and editing the directory; no privileged plans

In 'active', the passphrase opens recovery only for the recorded administrator's stable user ID. Recovery permits exactly: enrolling replacement administrator credentials without an existing hardware check (the D16 exception) and revoking credentials. Entering recovery bumps the global epoch (every assurance cookie stops working), revokes sessions, challenges, frozen plans, and outstanding tokens, publishes the snapshot, and is audited

Recovery → active only when the administrator again meets D11 and completes a fresh ceremony with an attested hardware key; until then no privileged plan, config change, or administrator grant is possible

'homebase admin reset' (root shell) revokes all administrator credentials and sessions, bumps the global epoch, sets a new passphrase, and returns to 'setup'; '--administrator <login>' records a different tailnet account as administrator when the old one is gone; audited

Every enrollment by a member with no usable credentials (none, or only orphaned or demoted ones) needs an enrollment grant: single-use, issued by the administrator for that member, expires in 15 minutes

Home Base writes the snapshot (generation, written_at, global epoch, cookie-verification public keys, members, roles, epochs, app access; no credentials) per D18 on every change and every 30 s; revoking a credential, disabling a member, or changing access bumps the generation and the member's epoch, so a revoked cookie stops working within ~5 s while Home Base is up
The administrator flag is local to this host and excluded from any future export/sync
userStories.testStrategy: State-machine tests for every transition, including passphrase use while active by the administrator and by anyone else, and recovery → active; transactional last-administrator test; revocation while apps keep running; Home Base stopped (apps refuse after 120 s); a snapshot made writable or symlinked is refused; login-reassignment test; API authorization tests (no UI source assertions)

userStories.title: Suite passkey service
acceptanceCriteria: Served by Home Base on its own socket and mounted at /_sovereign/auth/ on the Home Base and sensitive-app hostnames only (never svc:<instance>-home), so each of those hostnames sets its own host-only cookie (D21)

Members enroll multiple credentials (label, kind, AAGUID, transports, created/last-used) and revoke them, per the assurance policy matrix, on the Home Base hostname only (D21); enrollment and revocation requests on any other hostname are refused before a ceremony starts

Kind (D15): 'hardware' only with 'packed' attestation whose chain verifies to a root pinned in sovereignAuth; Home Base refuses to classify anything as hardware when no roots are loaded (the library would otherwise skip chain checks); self-attestation or an unpinned chain ⇒ not hardware. Each credential records the root it verified against

Pinned roots are updated through sovereignAuth releases; removing a root (e.g. vendor compromise) demotes credentials that verified against it on the next snapshot, and an administrator left without an attested hardware key is told to enroll a new one

Ceremonies use RP ID = the tailnet domain (D17), userVerification required, no PRF. Each challenge is stored with {issuing hostname, member, purpose, audience, action context, expiry}; finish verifies the assertion's origin, member, and purpose against that record, consumes it once, and refuses a challenge used on another hostname or for another purpose. clientDataJSON with crossOrigin true or any topOrigin is refused. A ceremony's cookie or token is never valid on another hostname

Attestation is requested ('direct') only when enrolling an administrator hardware key; ordinary enrollment requests 'none', because with roots pinned an unpinned packed chain is rejected outright rather than downgraded

Successful checks set a __Host-sv_assurance cookie (Secure, Path=/, no Domain, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict): Ed25519-signed {sub (stable user ID), aud (hostname), sid, cred, kind, epoch, auth_time}. The __Host- prefix is required because sibling hostnames are same-site and can otherwise plant cookies (D20)

Every-time tokens are minted only from a fresh ceremony and bind {sub, household, aud app, action, resolved target, digest}. For Home Base plans the digest is of the frozen plan (e.g. restore resolves 'latest' to a named backup before the 401) and the retry runs exactly that frozen plan; for apps it covers the canonical request body plus the target the app resolved. 60-second expiry; consumed atomically in SQLite (one consumption across processes and restarts)

The shared helper (/_sovereign/auth/stepup.js) turns a 401 step_up_required into its own confirm tap (iOS gesture), the ceremony, and one retry of the identical request; it never retries a request that changed
Signing-key rotation keeps the previous public key in the snapshot for one session window; losing the key invalidates sessions only
Members can see their check status (which credential, how long ago)
userStories.testStrategy: Unit tests for classification, cookie and token rules; concurrent redemption from two processes, restart, changed body, changed target ('latest' moved during the ceremony), cross-app redemption, redemption socket timeout; Playwright virtual-authenticator flows; attestation tests (pinned root passes; no roots loaded, self-attestation, and a valid chain to an unpinned root are not hardware; root removal demotes); VM rehearsal with real 1Password, Apple Passwords, and a hardware key on macOS and iOS; cross-host challenge/finish swap, purpose swap, replay, and member mismatch refused; ceremony and enrollment requests on svc:<instance>-home refused (route absent); crossOrigin/topOrigin assertions refused

userStories.title: Home Base admin on tailnet identity + passkeys
acceptanceCriteria: Home Base admin moves to svc:<instance>-homebase behind its nginx socket (D14); no TCP listener; :3080 is retired after a redirect period. Home Base also serves the nginx-only identity endpoint (D1) and the per-app redemption sockets (D19)

A route authorization matrix covers every Home Base route (reads and mutations: config, publishing, directory, roles, access, enrollment grants, recovery, plans, credential self-service) with its required level from the assurance policy, and classifies each as member self-service (acts only on the caller's own credentials or grant, checked by stable user ID), or administrator; a test fails if a route is missing, and a member is refused every administrator route and every other member's credentials (D21)
Every mutation uses the mutation guard; authorization runs before any mutation or step-up prompt; this closes the unauthenticated config route (bugBase #150) if it is not fixed sooner
Admin unlock requires the administrator's identity plus a passkey (8h session bound to the stable user ID and hostname)
Administrator actions and privileged plans need an every-time attested hardware key, bound to the plan's digest
userStories.testStrategy: Route-matrix completeness test; API authorization tests per route; cross-site form and sibling-hostname request tests; VM rehearsal of setup, active, recovery, and reset

The finance app runs as the sensitive canary on its own hostname and user: 30-day session, recent checks for linking accounts and exports, kid views at tailnet level (D7)

Local credentials stay intact and usable in local mode until after the feature's rollback window

userStories.title: Rollout runbook and VM rehearsal
acceptanceCriteria: docs/suite-identity-rollout-runbook.md covers read-only pre-checks, tailnet policy and service definitions, dependency-ordered cutover and rollback, verification, and the tailnet-rename re-enrollment procedure

The rehearsal repeats spike 3b and proves detection before cleanup: with a signed second node approved under a shared approver tag, the approvers are tightened and D23 must report the service unverified (automatic) while the stale approval still exists; then the approval is removed in the console, D23 passes, and the second node gets no traffic on drain. It also runs the no-API confirmation path from a fresh setup state (homebase-only publish, enrollment, then confirmation with the hardware key) and the D20/D21/D22 browser-isolation checks against the real apps
A full rehearsal on a test VM passes the spike-1, spike-2, and spike-3 checklists, an interrupted cutover, and a rollback, before any production host changes
Spike-only tailnet grants are removed after the rehearsal

followUpFeatures: App waves, each in its own app repo: wave 1 remaining low-friction apps (fasting, help desk, calendar, and whichever wasn't the pilot); wave 2 passphrase apps (home ops, photos, estate documents); wave 3 operator apps (trading, Bitcoin accounting) with the Python port of sovereignAuth

high: Any remaining TCP path to nginx or an app makes identity headers forgeable; the planner must refuse tailnet mode unless the socket-only path is in place, on both deployment paths

Low-friction apps share one hostname and one service user, so a compromised one can act as any member who visits it within that hostname; accepted, because those apps hold no sensitive data, and that hostname has no /_sovereign/auth/ mount, ceremonies, or assurance cookies (D21)
Administrator lockout if all credentials are lost; recovery and reset must be rehearsed

Service-host approval is a tailnet-policy boundary (spike 3b): an approved second host silently stands by and takes the service, its certificate, and members' identity headers on failover, and tightening the policy leaves its approval in place. Mitigated by per-host tags, per-service approvers, Tailnet Lock (D14), and D23, which decides on the service's complete host inventory; Tailnet Lock does not help against a host that is already signed, and the no-API branch rests on the administrator's confirmation
medium: Every request now depends on the Home Base identity endpoint; if Home Base is down, tailnet-mode apps see no identity until it returns (fail closed). Keep the endpoint small, cached per client IP for seconds, and separate from the admin process's heavy work
Each new hostname is an instance-qualified Tailscale Service that needs a tailnet policy entry and approval; more setup for other households
Renaming the tailnet invalidates every passkey (RP ID); the runbook's re-enrollment procedure is the only path
iOS requires a fresh user gesture for WebAuthn; the shared helper must keep its own confirm tap
Kids' surfaces must not regress; wave 1 must be invisible to kids except for removing the picker
If Home Base stops writing the snapshot, tailnet-mode apps refuse members once it ages out; max age must balance revocation speed against outages

Service hostnames are one browser site (D20): a compromised low-friction app can send credentialed requests and plant unprefixed cookies on sensitive hostnames. Mitigated by the exact-Origin, __Host-, aud, side-effect-free GET and resource-isolation rules; every new route needs those tests
Households without a Tailscale API credential rely on the administrator's periodic confirmation (D23) rather than automatic verification
Refusing requests without fetch metadata excludes clients older than Safari 16.4 / Chrome 80 / Firefox 90 on sensitive and Home Base hostnames (D20)
low: Hardware vendors outside the pinned roots can't serve as administrator hardware keys until their root is added
